Incident history (4)

📅 2026-10-14 Siege / Encirclement — Unspecified — Evacuated/Evacuation order INC-311
PROS AI Quds Hospital Is offering life-saving services to a large number of Palestinian patients and wounded, including critical cases in the Intensive Care Unit (ICU) and Children in incubators; in addition to hundreds of civilians who took refuge at the hospital. Accordingly, PRCS cannot evacuate the hospital, and by its humanitarian mandate is bound to continue the provision of services to the sick and wounded.

The Palestine Red Crescent Society (PRCS) was commanded by the Israeli Occupation Forces to evacuate PRCS Al Quds Hospital in Gaza City. The first deadline for evacuation was given to 06:00 a.m. of Saturday (14.10.2023), and then at mid-day Saturday a renewed deadline to evacuate by 16:00 hrs. Saturday (14.10.2023).

Sources: 🔗 reliefweb 🔗 reliefweb

📅 2023-11-10 Gunfire / Shooting — Direct hit — Access limited INC-315
At least one Palestinian was killed and 28 others injured by Israeli snipers

At least one Palestinian was killed and 28 others injured as Israeli snipers targeted displaced people at the Al-Quds Hospital in Gaza City, according to the Palestinian Red Crescent. In a statement, the aid organization took note of a "martyr and 20 injuries among the displaced, mostly children, with two of them in critical condition due to the occupation snipers targeting Al-Quds Hospital and firing directly at those displaced people in the building."

1 killed28 injured

📅 2023-11-08 Gunfire / Shooting — Direct hit — Access limited INC-314
One person was killed and 28 others were wounded in a shooting by Israeli forces.

Israeli forces opened fire on the intensive care unit at al-Quds hospital in Gaza City on Friday. One person was killed and 28 others were wounded in sniper fire by Israeli forces at the hospital, the PCRS said. The majority of the injured were children and two are in critical condition as a result of sniper fire targeting the hospital, a Red Crescent statement said.

1 killed28 injured
Sources: 🔗 theguardian 🔗 reuters
